label: Update gate drops at D1 after a rare a1-to-S2 trial, more so late in episode.
short_terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_action - prev_state == -1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action - prev_state == -1) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) * ep_trial
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_state == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_state == 2) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("action",-2) == 1) * (tv("state",-2) == 2) ;; (phase != D1) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 0)
explanation: z21 sits near 1 (keep the old state) on GO and D2 and on most D1 steps. At D1 it falls by about 0.3 when the previous trial was the rare a1->S2 transition, whether or not it was rewarded, so the unit lets in a new state only after that one rare pattern; the drop gets deeper later in the episode. After trials that reached S1 it sits slightly higher at D1. Reward, belief and the trial before add little: the a1->S2 indicator alone gives dev R2 0.56 beyond timing, and the 3-term short form gives 0.68, matching or beating the 8-term free fit (0.64 without the S1 term). The misses left are late-episode D1 drops after other patterns.

issues: The core claim holds. In the profile's D1 residuals the gate sits about -0.30 after a previous a1->S2 trial (r: -0.297, u: -0.311), so reward really doesn't matter. Every other D1 previous-trial cell is between 0 and +0.07, and GO/D2 residuals stay within about 0.01. The a1->S2 indicator alone scores 0.547 on test, and adding its ep_trial interaction raises that to 0.612, which confirms 'deeper later in the episode'.

The label leaves out the third short-form term, D1*(prev_state==1). It is worth +0.057 test R^2 (0.612 -> 0.669), with a weight of +0.054, so a reader of the label alone would not predict the small rise after S1 trials.

The third term works better as a late-episode effect. Replacing D1*(prev_state==1) with D1*(prev_state==1)*ep_trial raises test R^2 from 0.669 to 0.684. With that change, a short form without the plain a1->S2 indicator (2 terms, both scaled by ep_trial) already scores 0.669.

There is a remaining systematic miss class. The worst-fit dev windows are late-episode (t>=90) D1 steps where z falls steadily over runs of trials that are not a1->S2, for example repeated a2 S2 common unrewarded trials (0.72 -> 0.49 -> 0.29 -> 0.18, predicted 0.83). The cell-mean errors are small (largest is D1 after a2 S2 r, +0.027), so this is a late-episode drift and not a misassigned cell. The explanation already admits it.

The term prev_action - prev_state == -1 is an opaque way to write 'previous trial was a1->S2'. It is exact, not curve fitting, and it is needed to stay within the 3-factor limit when multiplied by ep_trial.
Belief and the trial before add almost nothing, as claimed. Adding D1*belief_lo gives 0.617 and tv(-2) a1S2 gives 0.612, both against 0.612 without them. No future variables are used.
